rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Closest candidate, not a violation: chunk 2 "GitHub Issues" line 30: "so `gh` covers what the MCP server covers for nearly every practical task" uses "the MCP server" before "the official GitHub MCP server" is named by full title (line 32). Resolves against the chunk's own header (GitHub Issues) plus the generic "MCP server" concept already established in chunk 1 (line 12: "Install an MCP server directly") — one plausible candidate in a GitHub-scoped section, not two. Harm (a referent the reader can't place) is absent.

No callback to another curriculum file by position anywhere in the body; all internal cross-references are external product URLs (github.com, atlassian.com, linear.app) or same-file section names ("Plugins and marketplaces on this page", line 15), not other deck files.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No "the X you did/saw" backward beat reference anywhere in the body — this is a flat lookup page, not an exercise/lecture with a module beat history.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No guess/predict-then-reveal demo beat in this file; it is install-command lookup content, no live-demo shape present.

Every chunk carries a self-carrying claim, including the shortest (chunk 5 "Other trackers", 31w): "Check the Anthropic Directory for reviewed connectors and your tracker's own docs. Most have a third-party MCP or a CLI fallback (like `gh`)." is a complete, standalone claim, not a wait-state bullet.

Checked all 7 headed chunks against their content: e.g. chunk 6 header "Plugins and marketplaces: MCP servers bundled for distribution" (line 89) is literally true of its content (plugin/.mcp.json mechanism, marketplace install commands); chunk 7 header "What Claude Code doesn't do yet" (line 112) matches its three-bullet gap list. No header contradicted by its chunk's content.

No "Not X. Not Y. Z." construction found (grepped body for 'Not '). No anaphora/epistrophe triples. No verb triplets with an empty leg. No number-with-retraction pattern. Closest self-grading-superlative candidate: chunk 4 line 77 "Cleanest UX of the three trackers for solo engineers, regardless of path." — this grades a third-party product (Linear) against its competitors, not our own training/exercise value, so it is not the value-prop-leak shape §7 and check_writing.md §13 target (the exercise proving usefulness, not the reference page). Harm absent; stays PASS.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This file is a lookup surface (opens "Flat lookup", line 3) so the reference-page waiver lifts the per-slide bold-count budget — the handle cap still binds (≲5 words, label not sentence). Multiple bolds run full descriptive sentences well past that cap: chunk 3 "Jira" line 50 "**CLI install (when you want project scope or a different Claude.ai account):**" = 12 words; chunk 3 line 60 "**individual engineers don't need per-install admin approval**" = 7 words, mid-paragraph emphasis of a claim rather than a label at all; chunk 2 "GitHub Issues" line 32 "**When to add the official GitHub MCP server instead.**" = 9 words; chunk 6 "Plugins and marketplaces" line 108 "**When to reach for plugin distribution over plain `claude mcp add`.**" = 11 words, line 95 "**Add a marketplace, then install a plugin:**" = 7 words; chunk 4 "Linear" line 79 "**Fallbacks when a tenant blocks the first-party server:**" = 8 words; chunk 1 line 12 "**`claude mcp add` from the command line.**" = 7 words (borderline — functions as a parallel list-item title alongside two in-cap siblings, but still over the literal count). Already logged: `curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/pre-cohort-todos.md` lines 59 and 73 record this exact finding ("trim the whole-sentence bolds in chunks 2/3/4/6").
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Trim each flagged bold to its label/title alone (e.g. "CLI install:" not the parenthetical after it); move the descriptive clause to plain text.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: This is a standalone reference page (surface-type reference, not inlined into a module via an include-link the way exercises/lectures are — confirmed via `grep -rn mcp-and-connectors curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/*.md curriculum/exercises/*.md`, which shows only navigational pointer links, e.g. `getting-going.md:123` and `close-the-ticket.md:35`, never an include). The module-deck phase/section-wrapper drop mechanism rule 10 targets does not apply to a page rendered on its own; no cross-file presence claim is being made in this body.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
rules_evaluated.evidence: No `## Phase N:` / `## N.` step headers in this file (headers are topic labels, e.g. "Jira: Atlassian Rovo MCP (official)"), so the header-numbering mechanism is N/A; ran `node scripts/check-slide-numbering.js` over the training and it returned zero output for this file (no flags). Content ordinals "Path 1"/"Path 2"/"Path 3" (inline list, not headers) are used consistently throughout: Path 1 = Claude.ai inheritance (lines 11, 40, 108), Path 2 = `claude mcp add` (lines 12, 15, 32, 34, 93, 108), Path 3 = first-party CLI (lines 13, 23, 32) — every later reference resolves to the correct original definition.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Page geometry dies at the cut; reading order survives.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-deixis.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md` → "OK — 1 files, no page-geometry pointers across the slide cut." Closest candidate reviewed by hand: chunk 1 line 15 "under *Plugins and marketplaces* on this page" names the target section by title (the rule's own preferred fix) rather than by geometric position (no "below/above/further down"); "this page" reads as "this document", which stays true whether the file renders as long-read or as a multi-slide deck.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Slide size — 210 words / 6 bullets, and the cap is machine-checked.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Ran `node scripts/check-slide-size.js --file curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md --report` → exit 1, "oversized: 1", "trainings/agentic-engineering-101/reference/mcp-and-connectors.md:89 [395w] ## Plugins and marketplaces: MCP servers bundled for distribution". This slide is 395w against the 210w cap (fenced code already excluded by the tool). Note for the record: the training-wide sweep (`node scripts/check-slide-size.js`, no `--file`) reports "oversized: 0" across 45 files/266 slides, but that sweep's file set is built only from module include-links (`fileSetFromTraining` in `scripts/check-slide-size.js`) and this reference page is never included in it (confirmed: it does not appear in `--report`'s full listing) — so the training-wide "0 oversized" figure says nothing about this file; the `--file` run against the file directly is the one that actually measured it, and it fails. Grepped the maintainer block: no `**Slide size accepted:** ## Plugins and marketplaces...` accept-note exists. Already logged: `pre-cohort-todos.md` lines 59 and 73 record this exact 395w finding and prescribe a split.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Split `## Plugins and marketplaces` into two chunks (e.g. plugin/marketplace mechanism vs. install commands + when-to-use), or add a `**Slide size accepted:**` maintainer accept-note if the split is rejected.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Heading grammar is the mood switch, and it is load-bearing.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Rule 15 defines grammar conventions for exercise headings (imperative/phase label) and lecture headings (claims); this file is a third surface type (quick reference / flat lookup), which the rule does not assign a grammar convention to. Headers here are topic labels ("GitHub Issues", "Jira: Atlassian Rovo MCP (official)") consistent with a lookup page's own function, not a mismatch against either defined convention.
